explanation: A Christian apostle who was imprisoned during the journey described in the chapter, known for his faithfulness and ability to encourage others in difficult times.
The powerful northeasterly wind (Euraquilo) that drove the ship off course and threatened to sink it in the Mediterranean Sea.
The man responsible for steering the crew, navigation, and safety of the ship during the dangerous voyage to Italy.
The sailors on board who worked hard to save the cargo and the ship by throwing goods overboard and setting up sails in the storm.
Now known as Malta, the island where the ship ran aground after being driven onto a sandbar during the hurricane.
Paul's status as a Roman prisoner who was bound to soldiers and transported to stand trial in Rome.
